newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch-May 22.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch-May 22.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Thursday morning:
** India has emerged as the world's third most preferred destination for foreign direct investment in the medium term of five to ten years, the Business Standard reports.
The paper says Indian stands behind only China and the United States, according to a survey of global executives conducted by the Wordl Economic Forum in its Global Competitiveness Report 1997.
** The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) said on Wednesday it has filed a petition to wind up troubled finance firm CRB Capital Markets Ltd.
"The RBI has filed a wind-up petition against CRB Capital Markets," the central bank said in a statement.
The move came after firm chairman C.R. Bhansali failed to meet central bank officials to explain discrepancies in the company's operations and how he planned to repay depositors.
** BAT Industries has acquired proxies from Rothmans group of UK, which holds about 1.5 percent in ITC Ltd., the daily Economic Times says.
The paper says with the acquiring of the proxies, BAT group's effective control in ITC has increased to 33 percent.
** Focus on tobacco conglomerate ITC Industries which has taken a hit after posting lower-than-expected profits. ITC shares on Wednesday slid 20.0 rupees to 419.0.
** Activity seen in Container Corporation which announced a higher net profit of 968.0 million rupees in 1996/97 (March-April) against 522.3 million last year.
** Bombay's benchmark 30-share index closed 33.29 points, or 0.88 percent down at 3,735.01.
** The National Stock Exchange index fell 8.85 points at 1,042.0.
